chapter.name: Grassroots Democracy -- Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas

questions.q: A class poster copies the governance pyramid of Fig. 12.2 with only three levels. The top card reads 'Union Government' and the bottom card reads 'Local Government'. Which card belongs in the middle?
questions.a: State Government

questions.q: The chapter opens with words spoken by Rustom K. Sidhwa on 13 October 1949. Of which body was he a member?
questions.a: The Constituent Assembly

questions.q: The chapter describes participatory democracy as citizens actively taking part in their country's functioning at the rural, regional, urban, state or national level. Which of these is an example of it at the URBAN level?
questions.a: Residents of a Bhubaneswar colony tell their ward committee where a public toilet is needed.
o: Residents of a Bhubaneswar colony tell their ward committee where a public toilet is needed.
Members of a village Gram Sabha meet together to discuss repairs to the roof of the village school.
Residents of a city colony leave every decision about their lane to officials and never raise any problem.
A city newspaper prints a full list of the names of all the ministers of the State Government.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In the chapter's governance pyramid, the State Government forms the base of the pyramid.
Reason (R): The base of the pyramid is the local level, closer to the people, while the top is the national level.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.q:
(a) Into which two branches does Local Government divide in the chapter's governance pyramid (Fig. 12.2)?
(b) Which of these two branches does Chapter 12 explore?
questions.a: (a) Panchayati Raj Institutions on the rural side and Urban Local Bodies on the urban side. (b) Urban Local Bodies, the right side of the pyramid; the rural side was explored in Chapter 11.
s: (a) Names both branches: Panchayati Raj Institutions (rural) and Urban Local Bodies (urban)
(b) States that Chapter 12 explores Urban Local Bodies

questions.q:
Sidhwa said a local body should be formed 'so that people may know really what is an administration, what are the franchise, what are the powers, what are the rights and what are the privileges in a small sphere, in their own town, in their own villages.'
(a) What kind of local body did he want to be formed immediately?
(b) Name any two things he wanted people to learn about.
(c) Which two places did he mean by the 'small sphere'?
questions.a: (a) A full-fledged local body. (b) Any two of: what an administration is, the franchise, the powers, the rights, the privileges. (c) The people's own town and their own villages.
s: (a) A full-fledged local body
(b) Any two of administration, franchise, powers, rights, privileges
(c) Their own town and their own villages

questions.q:
Consider these statements about the chapter's introduction and its governance pyramid.
I. The Introduction names only three levels at which citizens can take part: rural, urban and national.
II. The chapter says it will limit itself to the basic principles of the urban governance system.
III. The Gram Sabha appears on the urban side of the pyramid, below the Ward Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.a: II only

questions.q: Tanvi says: 'Local Government sits at the base of the governance pyramid, so it must be the least important level of government.' Is she right? Give three points from the chapter.
questions.a: She is not right. (1) In the chapter the base of the pyramid shows the local level, the one closest to the people; the pyramid shows where each level sits, from local to national, not which is least important. (2) One of the chapter's two Big Questions asks why urban local bodies are important in governance and democracy. (3) Sidhwa wanted a full-fledged local body formed immediately so that people could learn about administration, powers and rights in their own town or village.
s: Says she is not right: the base stands for the level closest to the people, not the least important
Uses the Big Question on why urban local bodies are important in governance and democracy
Uses Sidhwa's call for a full-fledged local body to be formed immediately

questions.q: Sort these eight bodies into the two branches of Local Government shown in the chapter, rural (Panchayati Raj Institutions) or urban (Urban Local Bodies): Zila Panchayat, Ward Committee, Gram Sabha, Municipal Corporation, Panchayat Samiti, Nagar Panchayat, Gram Panchayat, Municipal Council.
questions.a: Rural (Panchayati Raj Institutions): Zila Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Gram Panchayat, Gram Sabha. Urban (Urban Local Bodies): Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Nagar Panchayat, Ward Committee. The Nagar Panchayat is urban even though its name has 'Panchayat': it is the body of cities and towns with smaller populations.
s: Places Zila Panchayat and Panchayat Samiti under rural
Places Gram Panchayat and Gram Sabha under rural
Places Municipal Corporation and Municipal Council under urban
Places Nagar Panchayat and Ward Committee under urban

questions.q: In 1949 Sidhwa hoped that a local body would let people learn, 'in a small sphere', what administration, powers and rights really are. Evaluate, in five points, how far the urban local bodies described in this chapter make this possible for people living in a city. Use decentralisation, wards and ward committees, citizens' duties and elected members, and end with your own judgement.
questions.a: (1) Urban local bodies are decentralised: instead of a central authority at the top, local communities have a direct say on how their areas are managed, a way for citizens to come together and decide what is best for them. (2) Cities are divided into small units called wards; ward committees run health camps and campaigns against single-use plastics and report problems such as a water leak or a blocked drain, so people see administration at work close to home. (3) Citizens have duties, such as following waste-segregation instructions and promptly reporting a water leakage, which makes it a participatory democracy. (4) As in villages, urban local bodies have elected members who represent the local citizens. (5) Judgement: largely yes, the chance Sidhwa wanted exists in a city, but the chapter also shows that cities are more complex and that people are more independent and often do not know their neighbours, so taking part 'seems more complicated'; people must use the chance, since everyone's voice matters.
s: Decentralisation: local communities get a direct say instead of a central authority
Wards and ward committees: activities and reporting of problems close to home
Citizens' duties (waste segregation, reporting leaks) in a participatory democracy
Elected members who represent local citizens, as in rural areas
A justified judgement that weighs the city's complexity and people not knowing neighbours

questions.q: Urban local bodies do not operate under a central authority at the top; instead, local communities have a direct say on how their areas are managed. Which word does the chapter use for this feature?
questions.a: Decentralised

questions.a: Conducting a health camp

Organising a campaign against single-use plastics

questions.a: False. Urban local bodies are decentralised: instead of operating under a central authority at the top, the local communities have a direct say on how their areas are managed and the issues they face.
s: Verdict: False
Correct statement: urban local bodies are decentralised, so local communities have a direct say on how their areas are managed

Reason (R): Ward committees organise campaigns against the use of single-use plastics.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.q:
Three residents of a ward in Ranchi bring their worries to the ward committee. Using the chapter, say what the committee could do in each case.
(a) Leela sees plastic carry bags littering the vegetable market every day.
(b) Imran notices water seeping out from a pipe under the footpath.
(c) Mrs Das wants check-ups for elderly residents who cannot travel far to a hospital.
questions.a: (a) Organise a campaign against the use of single-use plastics. (b) Keep an eye on the water leak and report it to the authorities. (c) Conduct a health camp in the ward.
s: (a) A campaign against single-use plastics
(b) Reports the water leak to the authorities
(c) Conducts a health camp

questions.q:
The ward committee of Ward 12 in Guwahati keeps a notebook. Its March entries read: 4 March: met 60 market shopkeepers to ask them to stop handing out single-use plastic bags. 11 March: drain near the primary school found blocked. 18 March: free health camp in the community hall, 210 residents came. 25 March: water leaking from the main pipe on Station Road. For April, the committee has volunteers for only one big event: a second health camp or a second plastics drive.
(a) Which two entries are activities the committee facilitates, and which two are problems it keeps an eye on?
(b) According to the chapter, what should the committee do about the 11 March and 25 March entries?
(c) A new member who moved from another State says ward committees there worked a little differently. Is one of the two places doing it wrongly? Give the chapter's reason.
(d) Which event should the committee hold in April? Justify your choice using the March data.
questions.a: (a) Facilitated activities: the plastics drive (4 March) and the health camp (18 March). Problems watched: the blocked drain (11 March) and the water leak (25 March). (b) Report both problems to the authorities. (c) No; the precise functioning of wards differs from State to State, depending on the rules each State makes. (d) Either choice, if justified with the data: the health camp, because 210 residents came in March, showing strong demand; or the plastics drive, because 60 shopkeepers who serve many customers can cut single-use plastics for the whole market.
s: (a) Sorts the plastics drive and health camp as activities, the drain and leak as problems watched
(b) Reports both problems to the authorities
(c) No: the functioning of wards differs from State to State by each State's rules
(d) Chooses one event and justifies it with the March data

questions.q:
Consider these statements about wards and ward committees.
I. Ward committees decide the rules for how wards work across their whole State.
II. A ward committee may organise a campaign against the use of single-use plastics.
III. Ward committees report problems such as a blocked drain to the authorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.a: II and III only

questions.q: Rohan says: 'Ward committees make city government decentralised, because they take the place of the urban local bodies.' Is he right, wrong or partly right? Give three points from the chapter.
questions.a: Partly right. (1) Right: ward committees bring decisions close to the people of a ward; they facilitate activities such as health camps and watch for problems, which fits decentralisation, where local communities have a direct say. (2) Wrong: in Fig. 12.2 the Ward Committee sits below the urban local bodies (Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council or Nagar Panchayat) and above the People of the Ward, so it is part of the urban system, not a replacement for it. (3) Wrong: a ward committee reports problems such as a water leak to the authorities instead of handling everything itself.
s: Verdict partly right, with what is right: ward committees bring decisions close to the ward's people
Uses Fig. 12.2: the Ward Committee sits below the urban local bodies, not in their place
Uses the fact that ward committees report problems to the authorities

questions.a: Garbage collection and disposal

questions.a: Reporting a water leak in the street promptly

Consider these statements about urban local bodies and citizens.
I. The chapter gives urban local bodies some role in planning for the area's economic and social development.
II. According to the chapter, promptly reporting a water leakage is a function of the urban local body, not a duty of citizens.
III. Maintaining the burial ground is one of the functions of urban local bodies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.a: I and III only

questions.q:
In Ritu's apartment block, each floor has separate bins for wet and dry waste, but most families throw all their waste into one bin.
(a) Which duty of citizens named in the chapter are these families not performing?
(b) Using (a), explain how this affects the work of the urban local body.
questions.a: (a) Carefully following the instructions on waste segregation. (b) When waste is not segregated, garbage collection becomes harder; the chapter says urban local bodies can perform their functions efficiently only if the people living in the city also perform their duties.
s: (a) Following instructions on waste segregation
(b) Garbage collection becomes harder, so the body cannot work efficiently without citizens doing their duties

questions.q: True or False? 'Collecting local taxes and fines is one of the functions of urban local bodies.' Give the verdict and a reason from the chapter.
questions.a: True. The chapter lists collecting local taxes and fines among the functions of urban local bodies, along with taking care of the infrastructure, maintaining the burial ground, garbage collection and disposal, and checking the implementation of government schemes.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: the chapter lists it among the functions of urban local bodies

questions.q:
Name the function of urban local bodies, from the chapter's list, that each of these jobs shows.
(a) Workers repave a potholed road leading to a city market.
(b) The city body keeps the burial ground near the river clean and in repair.
(c) The city body draws up a plan for new markets and a skills centre to help the area grow.
questions.a: (a) Helping take care of the infrastructure. (b) Maintaining the burial ground. (c) Planning for the area's economic and social development.
s: (a) Taking care of the infrastructure
(b) Maintaining the burial ground
(c) Planning for the area's economic and social development

questions.q: Neha says: 'If the city body has enough trucks and workers, residents need not bother about separating their waste.' Test her claim against the chapter. Give three points.
questions.a: Her claim is wrong. (1) The chapter says that for urban local bodies to perform their functions efficiently, the people living in the city must also perform their duties. (2) It says that when people carefully follow instructions on waste segregation, garbage collection becomes easier; more trucks do not do the separating. (3) It reminds us that this is a participatory democracy, so people must show care and concern for their area.
s: Verdict wrong: bodies work efficiently only when citizens also do their duties
Waste segregation makes garbage collection easier
Participatory democracy: citizens must show care and concern for their area

questions.q:
A housing colony in Coimbatore has 240 households. The city body's garbage van crew takes 2 minutes to load the waste of a household that has separated wet and dry waste, and 5 minutes for a household that has not. In May, 90 households separated their waste and the other 150 did not. The residents' association wants the daily collection to take less time.
(a) Which function of urban local bodies is the van crew carrying out?
(b) Which duty of citizens, named in the chapter, decides how long the crew takes at each house?
(c) How many minutes of loading did the colony need each day in May, and how many would it need if all 240 households separated their waste?
(d) The association can either ask the city body for a second van or run a drive to get every household to separate its waste. Which should it try first? Justify using (c) and the chapter.
questions.a: (a) Garbage collection and disposal. (b) Following instructions on waste segregation. (c) May: 90 x 2 + 150 x 5 = 180 + 750 = 930 minutes; if all 240 separate: 240 x 2 = 480 minutes. (d) The drive first: it would cut the loading time by 930 - 480 = 450 minutes (7 hours 30 minutes) a day without any new van, and the chapter says urban local bodies work efficiently only when citizens do their duties. A second van would share the 930 minutes between two crews but would not reduce the total work.
s: (a) Garbage collection and disposal
(b) Following waste-segregation instructions
(c) 930 minutes in May and 480 minutes if all separate
(d) Chooses the drive (saving 450 minutes a day) and links it to citizens' duties

questions.q:
A ward notice board lists four jobs. For each one, write whether it is a function of the urban local body or a duty of the residents, and give a reason from the chapter.
(i) Keeping wet and dry waste apart at home, as instructed.
(ii) Collecting local taxes from houses and shops.
(iii) Telling the ward office at once about a pipe leaking in the lane.
(iv) Checking that a government scheme reaches the people it is meant for.
questions.a: (i) Duty of residents: following waste-segregation instructions makes garbage collection easier. (ii) Function of the urban local body: collecting local taxes and fines is in its list of functions. (iii) Duty of residents: reporting a water leakage promptly prevents further wastage of water. (iv) Function of the urban local body: checking the implementation of government schemes is in its list.
s: (i) Duty: waste segregation makes garbage collection easier
(ii) Function: collecting local taxes and fines
(iii) Duty: prompt reporting prevents further wastage of water
(iv) Function: checking the implementation of government schemes

questions.q: The Mehta family has just moved into a flat in Lucknow. Their ward committee is preparing a welcome leaflet for new residents. Write the leaflet's five points: three functions of the urban local body that the family will benefit from, each with an example from daily life, and two duties the family is expected to perform, each with what it achieves.
questions.a: Functions (any three, each with a daily-life example): taking care of the infrastructure (roads and footpaths repaired); garbage collection and disposal (waste picked up from the building); maintaining the burial ground; checking the implementation of government schemes; collecting local taxes and fines; planning for the area's economic and social development. Duties: following waste-segregation instructions, which makes garbage collection easier; promptly reporting a water leakage in the street, which prevents further wastage of precious water.
s: First function with a daily-life example
Second function with a daily-life example
Third function with a daily-life example
Waste segregation and how it makes garbage collection easier
Promptly reporting a water leakage and how it prevents wastage of water

questions.q: True or False? 'The Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai is older than the Greater Chennai Corporation.' Give the verdict and the reason, with years.
questions.a: False. The Greater Chennai Corporation was earlier the Madras Corporation, established in 1688, the oldest municipal institution in India; Mumbai's corporation was created in 1865, 177 years later.

Reason: Greater Chennai Corporation is the former Madras Corporation of 1688, older than Mumbai's 1865 corporation by 177 years

(b) 84 years
(c) 105 years

questions.q:
For a school exhibition, Class 6B is hanging five cards on a rope called 'How our local bodies began'. The cards hang in order of year: Card 1: 1687, Card 2: 1688, Card 3: 1792, Card 4: 1865, Card 5: 1949. Each card must carry one event from Chapter 12. The rope is short, and the teacher says one card may have to be removed.
(a) Write the events for Card 1 and Card 4.
(b) Which card shows the birth of India's oldest municipal institution, and what is that institution called today?
(c) Which card marks when municipal administration in Madras properly began, and why?
(d) If one card must go, which would you remove with the least loss to the story of how municipal bodies began? Justify your choice.
questions.a: (a) Card 1: the East India Company's charter makes Fort St. George and all territories within 16 km of it a corporation. Card 4: the Bombay Municipal Corporation (now the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai) is created. (b) Card 2: the Madras Corporation, now the Greater Chennai Corporation. (c) Card 3, 1792: a Parliamentary Act gave the corporation the power to levy municipal taxes, which is when municipal administration properly began. (d) A justified choice, for example Card 5: Sidhwa's 1949 words are a call for local bodies, while the other four cards mark real steps in setting up municipal bodies. (Removing Card 1 is acceptable if the student argues that Card 2 already shows the Madras Corporation's start.)
s: (a) Gives the 1687 charter event and the 1865 Bombay Municipal Corporation event
(b) Card 2, the Madras Corporation, now the Greater Chennai Corporation
(c) Card 3: the 1792 Act gave the power to levy municipal taxes
(d) Chooses one card and justifies it by what that event adds to the story

(b) Links it to collecting local taxes and fines
(c) Names two charges such as property tax and water charges, which help fund the body's services

II. A funeral van is among the 'CRM - Services on request' of the Indore Municipal Corporation.
III. The chapter says that its list of services offered by the Indore Municipal Corporation is simplified.

questions.a: I, II and III

questions.q:
Class 6 students of a school in Indore surveyed 400 households in their ward about waste. 352 households said they hand over wet and dry waste separately; the other households put all their waste into one bag. The students want the ward to reach 95% before their next survey. They have time for only one activity: a door-to-door visit to every household that does not separate its waste, or a talk at the school assembly for 600 students on the city's services.
(a) Under which government scheme has Indore been named India's cleanest city, and for how many years in a row?
(b) Under which heading of the Indore Municipal Corporation's list of services does dealing with the city's waste fall?
(c) What percentage of the surveyed households separate their waste now, and how many more must start to reach 95%?
(d) Which activity should the students choose? Justify using (c) and the chapter.
questions.a: (a) The Swachh Survekshan scheme, seven years in a row. (b) Solid waste management. (c) 352 / 400 x 100 = 88%; 95% of 400 is 380, so 380 - 352 = 28 more households. (d) Either, if justified: the door-to-door visit reaches exactly the 400 - 352 = 48 households that do not separate, and only 28 of them need to change, so it aims straight at the gap; the assembly talk reaches 600 students who can carry the message home to many families, but not necessarily to those 48. Both promote the citizen duty of following waste-segregation instructions, which makes garbage collection easier.
s: (a) Swachh Survekshan, seven years in a row
(b) Solid waste management
(c) 88% now and 28 more households
(d) Chooses an activity and justifies it using the 48 non-separating households or the reach of the talk

questions.q: Simran says: 'Chennai and Indore both have a Municipal Corporation at the top of their urban bodies, so each of them must have a population of more than 10 lakh.' Test her claim against the chapter. Give three points.

(2) It says only cities with a population above 10 lakh have a Municipal Corporation as their highest body; between 1 and 10 lakh it is a Municipal Council, and smaller places have a Nagar Panchayat. (3) So the type of body follows from population, and both cities must have more than 10 lakh people.
s: Verdict right: Chennai and Indore have a Municipal Corporation at the top
Only cities above 10 lakh have a Municipal Corporation as their highest body
Concludes that the type follows population, so both are above 10 lakh

questions.q:
Match each line from the dialogue in Column A with what it shows in Column B.
Column A: 1. 'People ... often don't even know their neighbours.'  2. 'We work together in the fields, celebrate festivals together.'  3. 'Dozens of people gathered ... to help clear the rubble.'  4. 'It sounds like our village Panchayat, only bigger.'
Column B: P. Sameer describing village life  Q. Sameer comparing rural and urban local bodies  R. Anita describing city life  S. Anita's example of community spirit in the city
True or False? 'In the dialogue, Sameer says that the members of his village Panchayat are elected, as the representatives in Anita's city are.' Give the verdict and support it from the dialogue.
questions.a: True. Anita says her city has local bodies and elected representatives who represent the people; Sameer replies that it sounds like his village Panchayat, only bigger, and that its members are elected too.
s: Verdict: True
Support: Anita mentions elected representatives and Sameer says Panchayat members are elected too

questions.q:
(a) Give two differences between city life and village life as Anita and Sameer describe them.
(b) Using the dialogue, show one thing that is the same in both places despite these differences.
questions.a: (a) Any two, for example: the city is busy, crowded and noisy with tall buildings, while the village is quiet; city people are more independent and often do not know their neighbours, while in the village everyone knows everyone and they work in the fields, celebrate festivals and make decisions together. (b) Any one: both have a sense of community (Anita's collapsed-house example in the city); both have elected representatives in their local government; in both, as Anita says, everyone's voice matters.
s: (a) Two differences between city and village life from the dialogue
(b) One thing the same in both, supported from the dialogue

questions.q: At the end of the dialogue Anita says that democracy 'seems more complicated in the city'. Give three reasons, from the dialogue and the rest of the chapter, why taking part in local government can seem harder in a city.
questions.a: (1) The city is busy and crowded, with many people rushing around all the time. (2) City people are more independent and often do not know their neighbours, while Sameer says that in the village, because everyone knows each other, a lot more people can take part and even children get heard. (3) The chapter says urban areas are generally more complex and diverse than rural ones, so the urban governance system is more complex too.
s: City is busy and crowded with people rushing around
People are independent and do not know neighbours, unlike the village where more people take part
Urban areas are more complex and diverse, so urban governance is more complex

questions.q:
During a monsoon storm in a lane of Varanasi, a tree branch fell across an electric wire. The wire sagged until it hung just above the tin roof of a tea shop. Four Class 6 students saw it on their way home from school. Instead of walking past, they went to a member of their ward committee who lives in the lane and explained the danger. Two days later the branch had been cleared and the wire lifted.
(a) Which branch of Local Government in the chapter's pyramid serves this lane?
(b) In Sameer's similar story, to whom did the village children explain their problem?
(c) Which point of the chapter's closing summary about citizens did the four students act on?
(d) Which idea in Anita's last words about democracy does this event support?
questions.a: (a) Urban Local Bodies (the urban side of the pyramid). (b) To one of their Gram Sabha members. (c) Citizens have duties to ensure that the local bodies are able to perform their functions efficiently; the students did theirs by reporting the problem promptly. (d) That the idea is the same in the city as in the village: everyone's voice matters.
s: (a) Urban Local Bodies
(b) A Gram Sabha member
(c) Citizens have duties that help local bodies work efficiently
(d) Everyone's voice matters, in the city as in the village

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Anita says there is still some sense of community in the city.
Reason (R): After heavy rains a house collapsed two streets away from her, and dozens of people gathered to help clear the rubble and make sure no one was trapped inside.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Sameer says that the city's local bodies sound 'like our village Panchayat, only bigger'. Evaluate his remark in four steps: where the chapter shows he is right, where the city system differs in more than size, how taking part differs between the two places, and your final judgement.
questions.a: (1) He is right that both have elected members who represent the local people: Anita speaks of elected representatives, Sameer says Panchayat members are elected too, and the closing summary says urban local bodies have elected members as in the rural context. (2) The city system is not just bigger: urban areas are more complex and diverse, so urban governance is more complex; a city is divided into wards with ward committees, and its highest body depends on population (Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council or Nagar Panchayat). (3) Taking part differs: in the village everyone knows each other, so many more people, even children, get heard, while city people are more independent and often do not know their neighbours. (4) Judgement: partly right. The idea is the same, since everyone's voice matters in both, but the city system differs in structure and in how people take part, not only in size.
s: Right: both have elected members who represent local people
City system differs beyond size: more complex, wards and ward committees, body type by population
Participation differs: village people know each other; city people often do not
Final judgement: partly right, same idea but more than a difference of size

questions.q: Your school is in a city of 18 lakh people and wants to start a 'Young Citizens Club'. Plan the club's work in five points: (i) name the city's highest urban local body, with the reason; (ii) say whom the club should tell first about a dangerous problem in its lane, and what that body will do; (iii) name one ward-committee activity the club could join; (iv) name one duty the club will encourage at home and what it achieves; (v) give one lesson from Sameer's story that the club should follow, and say why it matters in a city.
questions.a: (i) A Municipal Corporation (Mahanagar Nigam), because the city has more than 10 lakh people. (ii) The ward committee, which keeps an eye on problems such as a water leak, a blocked drain or a damaged road and reports them to the authorities. (iii) A health camp or a campaign against single-use plastics. (iv) Following waste-segregation instructions, which makes garbage collection easier (or promptly reporting a water leakage, which prevents further wastage of water). (v) Do not only report a problem; explain to a representative what should be done, as the village children did about shifting the electric post. This matters in a city because people often do not know their neighbours, so a club that speaks up together helps make sure everyone's voice is heard.
s: (i) Municipal Corporation, because the population is above 10 lakh
(ii) The ward committee, which reports such problems to the authorities
(iii) A health camp or a campaign against single-use plastics
(iv) A citizen duty such as waste segregation, with what it achieves
(v) A lesson from Sameer's story and why it matters where people often do not know their neighbours
